title: Enforce schema, required fields, tool permissions, and input contracts before semantic scoring while identifying requirements that structure alone cannot prove

questions.prompt: An agent can call a tool that immediately emails an attached document. The tool requires a recipient address and a document ID, and the agent may send only documents it has permission to share. A developer proposes checking these requirements only after the tool finishes, when validating the agent's final response. Explain why these checks must run before tool execution.

rubric.point: Required arguments and sharing permission determine whether the tool call is allowed to execute; they must be checked at the tool boundary.
Checking the final response cannot prevent or undo an email already sent, even if that response passes validation.

questions.model: Argument and sharing-permission checks must gate the tool call. Once the email is sent, a valid final response cannot undo an unauthorized disclosure.

source.heading: Forgetting to Check Tool Inputs, Not Just Outputs

questions.prompt: A support agent returns JSON containing a permitted action, `close_ticket`, and a nonempty reason. All required fields, argument contracts and permission checks pass. No executable rule specifies when closing a ticket resolves the customer's request. Why is semantic evaluation still needed?
options: The checks establish contract compliance; judging whether closing addresses the request needs assessment beyond those rules.
The checks establish contract compliance; semantic evaluation must authorize the action before the tool can execute.
The checks establish that closing is appropriate; semantic evaluation only needs to improve the reason's wording.
The checks establish that closing is appropriate; semantic evaluation must confirm that the JSON is parseable.

rubric.point: Identifies that contract compliance does not establish whether the permitted action addresses the customer's request.

questions.model: Contract compliance does not prove that closing the ticket addresses the customer's request; that decision is not encoded in the checks.
